claim: Roxadustat improves outcomes in anemia of chronic kidney disease
gold_rationale: Efficacy on the hematologic surrogate is not in dispute: across pivotal phase 3 RCTs roxadustat corrects hemoglobin and reduces transfusion need vs placebo (non-dialysis: Fishbane OLYMPUS JASN 2021, +1.75 vs +0.40 g/dL, 63% fewer transfusions, N=2781, NCT02174627) and is non-inferior to epoetin alfa in dialysis (Chen NEJM 2019, N=305, NCT02652806). What makes the benefit/risk genuinely CONTESTED is the cardiovascular/thromboembolic safety signal and the divergent regulatory verdicts. Industry-sponsored pooled phase 3 analyses report MACE non-inferiority (dialysis-dependent MACE HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.95-1.26, Barratt Adv Ther 2021; NDD vs placebo MACE HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.96-1.27, Provenzano CJASN 2021; NDD/ID-DD vs ESA MACE HR 0.79, Barratt 2023) — but independent meta-analysis (Abdelazeem PLoS One 2022) found significantly higher serious adverse events (RR 1.07), deep vein thrombosis (RR 3.80) and hypertension (RR 1.37) in NDD patients, and the largest independent pool (Tian Ren Fail 2024, 18 trials, 8806 pts) confirms CV-event neutrality but real NDD hypertension (RR 1.37 vs placebo) and DD hyperkalemia. The US FDA CRDAC voted 13-1 (NDD) and 12-2 (DD) against approval on 15 July 2021 over thrombotic/MACE risk and NDD hemoglobin overcorrection, and the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on 11 Aug 2021 requiring an additional trial — while the EMA (CHMP positive opinion) and China/Japan/Chile/South Korea approved it. Same efficacy data, opposite benefit-risk conclusions by major regulators = Contested. One frequently-cited supporting pooled analysis (incident-to-dialysis, Provenzano Kidney Int Rep 2020, PMID 33732976, reporting LOWER MACE HR 0.70) has since been RETRACTED and is excluded from the corpus.

baseline.text: Roxadustat clearly works on the anemia itself — it is an oral HIF-prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor that reliably raises hemoglobin and cuts transfusion requirements in CKD anemia, both in non-dialysis patients (vs placebo) and dialysis patients (non-inferior to epoetin alfa), while also improving iron utilization. But 'improves outcomes' as a whole is contested because of cardiovascular safety. Pooled manufacturer analyses argue MACE is non-inferior to ESAs/placebo, yet independent analyses flagged increased thromboembolism (notably vascular-access thrombosis and DVT) and hypertension, and hemoglobin overcorrection in non-dialysis patients. Crucially, the US FDA's advisory committee voted overwhelmingly against approval in 2021 (13-1 NDD, 12-2 dialysis) and the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter demanding a new trial, whereas the EMA, China and Japan approved it. So the efficacy answer is yes, but the net benefit/risk verdict is genuinely unsettled — hence No, it does not unambiguously 'improve outcomes.'

rows.citation: Fishbane S, El-Shahawy MA, Pecoits-Filho R, et al. Roxadustat for Treating Anemia in Patients with CKD Not on Dialysis: Results from a Randomized Phase 3 Study (OLYMPUS). J Am Soc Nephrol. 2021;32(3):737-755. DOI:10.1681/ASN.2020081150. NCT02174627.
rows.finding: Pivotal double-blind NDD-CKD RCT (N=2781; 1393 roxadustat / 1388 placebo). Hemoglobin change from baseline +1.75 g/dL (95% CI 1.68-1.81) roxadustat vs +0.40 g/dL placebo (p<0.001); 63% reduction in RBC transfusion risk (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.30-0.44). AE profile comparable to placebo. Supports the hemoglobin-correction half of the claim; outcome_match=false because Hb is a surrogate, not a hard CV outcome. Independently re-verified against the abstract: N, Hb deltas, and transfusion HR all match exactly.
rows.integrity_note: Real pivotal trial; establishes efficacy on the surrogate. CV safety not the primary endpoint here.

rows.citation: Chen N, Hao C, Liu BC, et al. Roxadustat Treatment for Anemia in Patients Undergoing Long-Term Dialysis. N Engl J Med. 2019;381(11):1011-1022. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1901713. NCT02652806.
rows.finding: Phase 3 RCT in China (registered NCT02652806, confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov = FG-4592 dialysis study, N=305, 204 roxadustat / 101 epoetin, 2:1, 26 weeks). Roxadustat non-inferior to epoetin alfa for mean hemoglobin change (weeks 23-27; difference 0.2, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.5) and improved iron parameters. Confirms hemoglobin efficacy in the dialysis population. Surrogate endpoint (Hb), so outcome_match=false.
rows.integrity_note: Landmark NEJM pivotal; efficacy only, not powered for MACE. NCT02652806 verified as this exact trial (not ROCKIES).

rows.citation: Barratt J, Sulowicz W, Schomig M, et al. Efficacy and Cardiovascular Safety of Roxadustat in Dialysis-Dependent CKD: Pooled Analysis of Four Phase 3 Studies (PYRENEES, SIERRAS, HIMALAYAS, ROCKIES). Adv Ther. 2021;38(10):5345-5360. DOI:10.1007/s12325-021-01903-7.
rows.finding: Pooled 4 phase-3 open-label dialysis-dependent trials (N=4714; 2354 roxadustat / 2360 ESA). Hemoglobin non-inferior to ESA in each study; MACE HR 1.09 (95% CI 0.95-1.26), MACE+ HR 0.98 (0.86-1.11), all-cause mortality HR 1.13 (0.95-1.34) — non-inferior to ESA at prespecified 1.8/1.3 margins. Astellas/AstraZeneca-sponsored; addresses hard CV outcome (outcome_match=true). Numbers re-verified against abstract.
rows.integrity_note: Industry-authored, open-label; CIs cross 1 and upper bounds reach 1.26/1.34, consistent with 'no clear harm' but not a clean safety win — a key contested point. PubMed types it RCT/Phase III; 'meta-analysis of rcts' used as it is a pooled analysis of 4 trials.

rows.citation: Provenzano R, Fishbane S, Wei LJ, et al. Efficacy and Cardiovascular Safety of Roxadustat for Treatment of Anemia in Patients with Non-Dialysis-Dependent CKD: Pooled Results of Three Randomized Clinical Trials. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2021;16(8):1190-1200. DOI:10.2215/CJN.16191020. NCT01750190, NCT01887600, NCT02174627.
rows.finding: Pooled 3 placebo-controlled double-blind NDD-CKD trials (N=4277; roxadustat 2391 / placebo 1886). Hb averaged wk 28-52: 1.9 vs 0.2 g/dL (treatment diff 1.7, 95% CI 1.7-1.8); transfusion HR 0.26 (0.21-0.32). No increased MACE (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.96-1.27), MACE+ (HR 1.07, 0.94-1.21), or all-cause mortality (HR 1.08, 0.93-1.26) vs placebo. FibroGen/AstraZeneca-sponsored; reports MACE non-inferiority to placebo. All figures re-verified against abstract.
rows.integrity_note: Industry-authored; the same data the FDA panel reviewed and judged did not establish an adequate benefit-risk profile.

rows.citation: Abdelazeem B, Shehata J, Abbas KS, et al. The efficacy and safety of roxadustat for the treatment of anemia in non-dialysis dependent CKD: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs. PLoS One. 2022;17(4):e0266243. DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0266243.
rows.finding: Independent meta-analysis, 9 RCTs, NDD-CKD (roxadustat n=3175 vs control n=2446). Confirms large Hb increase (SMD 1.65) and improved iron indices, BUT roxadustat associated with significantly higher serious adverse events (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.13), deep vein thrombosis (RR 3.80, 95% CI 1.5-9.64; abstract p=0.08), and hypertension (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.13-1.65). Directly contradicts the CV-safety half of the claim. Numbers re-verified against abstract.
rows.integrity_note: Non-industry (typed Meta-Analysis/Systematic Review by PubMed); the DVT/thrombosis and hypertension signals are the crux of the contested benefit-risk balance. Note DVT p=0.08 despite CI excluding 1 (wide CI).

rows.citation: Barratt J, Dellanna F, Portoles J, et al. Safety of Roxadustat Versus ESAs in Non-Dialysis-Dependent or Incident-to-Dialysis CKD: Pooled Analysis of Four Phase 3 Studies (DOLOMITES, HIMALAYAS, SIERRAS, ROCKIES). Adv Ther. 2023;40(4):1546-1559. DOI:10.1007/s12325-023-02433-0.
rows.finding: Pooled 4 phase-3 open-label trials (N=2142; 1083 roxadustat / 1059 ESA). MACE HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.61-1.02), MACE+ HR 0.78 (0.62-0.98), all-cause mortality HR 0.78 (0.57-1.05) vs ESA — no increased CV/mortality risk. Astellas-sponsored, open-label. Direction 0: point estimates favor roxadustat but CIs mostly cross 1; treated as CV-neutral rather than a clear outcome improvement. Numbers re-verified. Abstract confirms ROCKIES = NCT02174731 (not NCT02652806).
rows.integrity_note: Industry-authored, open-label (unblinded) — adds to the 'non-inferior CV' evidence but methodologically weaker than the blinded placebo comparisons.

rows.citation: Tian L, Wang M, Liu M, et al. Cardiovascular and renal safety outcomes of the HIF prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor roxadustat for anemia patients with CKD: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Ren Fail. 2024;46(1):2313864. DOI:10.1080/0886022X.2024.2313864.
rows.finding: Independent meta-analysis, 18 trials (N=8806). No significant increase in cardiac-disorder risk vs placebo (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20) or ESA (RR 1.07, 0.92-1.24), in either DD (RR 1.09) or NDD (RR 1.04). BUT significantly increased hypertension in NDD (RR 1.20 vs ESA; RR 1.37 vs placebo) and hyperkalemia in DD. Net: CV-event-neutral but real adverse-effect signals — supports the 'contested', not 'clean-win', reading. All figures re-verified against abstract.
rows.integrity_note: Non-industry (Beijing academic authors); largest patient pool. Reinforces that MACE is roughly neutral while non-MACE harms (hypertension, hyperkalemia, and separately thrombosis) remain the safety concern.
